summary: Iteration 5 verifies since_days time-range diff feature + 'most_recent' recency-ordered list on /api/profile/{u}/following-list and /api/profile/{u}/followers-list, plus the rebuilt frontend Connections page (default tab 'Recently Followed', Time Range selector). Backend pytest: 31/31 tests pass individually (3 search tests transiently 429 when co-scheduled with the rate-limit test in the same xdist worker — confirmed passing after 60s window clear). New tests added: response contains {current, most_recent, added_details, removed_usernames, total_count, quota_exhausted, comparison_period, has_baseline, baseline_timestamp}; since_days=7 -> 'past 7 days'; since_days=0 -> 'last check'; since_days=1 -> 'past 1 day'; since_days=30 -> 'past 30 days'; since_days=400 -> 422; most_recent for followers = [] (server logic), most_recent for following = current[:20]. Live Apify follower/following data unavailable today — actor scraping_solutions~instagram-scraper-followers-following-no-cookies still on FREE_API_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED so `current=[], quota_exhausted=true` as expected. Frontend /connections page verified: default tab is 'Recently Followed' (active amber #d4a656), tab order 01 Recently Followed / 02 Followers / 03 Comments, Time Range dropdown visible with 'Past week' default and all 5 options (Past 24 hours, Past week, Past month, Past 3 months, Since last check). Time range hidden on Comments tab. Fetch Live Data click renders the amber 'Apify Daily Quota Reached' card gracefully. UI render-path for the non-quota-exhausted case validated by mocking the /following-list response with 24 users + 5 added + 2 removed — visually confirmed 3 StatCards (24 Total Following / +5 Followed in past 7 days / -2 Unfollowed in past 7 days), 'Followed in the past 7 days' section with #01..#05 rows and NEW badges (first 3 amber-highlighted), 'Most Recently Followed' section rendered below, and 'Unfollowed' pills. Scheduler now also calls _snapshot_connections(username,'following') daily — code path verified in server.py L521-542. Regression: /api/, /api/dashboard, /api/accounts (CRUD lifecycle), /api/profile/natgeo + cristiano, /api/profile/{u}/history, /api/profile/{u}/activity, /api/profile/{u}/post-comments, /api/relationships, /api/insights/{u}, /api/search, /api/image-proxy all pass. Rate limiting still enforced (60→200, 40→429 out of 100 /api/search requests).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py _snapshot_connections (L211-282): correctly uses timedelta cutoff and finds most recent snapshot on-or-before cutoff. For since_days=0 it falls back to the most recent snapshot regardless of age (comparison_period='last check') — good UX. Suggest also returning a `previous_snapshot_count` field so the UI can show 'baseline: 200 following on 2026-01-05'.
server.py L258: `if current_usernames:` guard prevents polluting snapshots with empty results — good fix from iteration_4 feedback.

server.py L270: `most_recent = current_list[:20] if connection_type == 'following' else []` — followers list intentionally returns empty most_recent because IG followers list is not reverse-chronological. This is correct but not documented in the endpoint docstring; consider adding a note.

server.py L536-542 scheduler now runs _snapshot_connections for 'following' daily — good. But `should_snapshot_following` check uses a 24h threshold and the scheduler itself runs every 6h, so effectively runs once every 24h per account. Consider aligning scheduler interval (e.g., 24h job for connections) or making the guard explicit.

server.py L538: scheduler passes since_days=7 to _snapshot_connections but since the scheduler's purpose is snapshot-only (not user-facing diff), the diff computation is wasted work. Consider a scheduler-only path that only inserts snapshot without computing diff.

Connections.js is 599 lines — approaching the 700-line threshold. Consider extracting FollowingView, FollowersView, UserRow, UserCard, StatCard, QuotaExhausted, CommentsView into separate files under /pages/connections/.

Connections.js line 246 `data.comparison_period` is trusted directly for user-facing labels; a malicious/proxy-modified server response could inject arbitrary text. Low risk since data comes from own backend, but worth wrapping in a whitelist check or React sanitization pattern.
Connections.js: `profile_pic` field is proxied via /api/image-proxy correctly. Fallback avatar (initial letter) also implemented. Good.

Connections.js: The default `tab='following'` state now matches the URL /connections without any deep-link tab param — if the user shares a URL, they always land on Recently Followed. Consider adding a `?tab=followers` query-param sync for shareability.

rca of the issue: Original user complaint 'still cant see who they recently followed, need to see in order of who they followed within like the past week' — root cause was two-fold: (a) endpoint did not support a time-window parameter, always diffing against the single most-recent snapshot; (b) UI did not surface Instagram's inherent recency ordering (position #1 = most recently followed) so even when data was available the user couldn't tell what was recent. Fix (verified this iteration): (a) added since_days query param (0..365) to both list endpoints, backend finds snapshot at/before now-since_days as baseline, returns comparison_period label + has_baseline + baseline_timestamp; (b) added most_recent = current_list[:20] for 'following' (IG follows list is reverse-chronological), rendered in frontend as 'Most Recently Followed' section with #NN numbered rows and amber highlight for top 3. Frontend default tab now 'Recently Followed'; Time Range selector defaults to 'Past week'. Verification blocked from live real-user data by Apify daily quota exhaustion — mocked-response test proves the render path works end-to-end.
